title: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving
summary: Off-road vision-language-action (VLA) models generate scene-conditioned plans, but frequent trajectory updates can repeatedly invoke expensive multimodal inference. Reusing a prediction reduces this demand while leaving its commands exposed to changes in vehicle motion. FastRoverVLA addresses this mismatch by decoupling visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution. Its training-free interface maintains decoded plans between visual predictions. A speed-curvature action buffer is aligned with measured motion at each update, integrated into a local trajectory, and advanced by consuming the current action. The corrected remainder is written back to the buffer, preserving motion corrections across successive updates. A bounded refresh rule normalizes speed and curvature variations within a newly decoded plan and assigns a short or long reuse budget according to the resulting plan-roughness score. The interface requires neither backbone features nor an additional learned driving policy. Over a 3 s horizon, independent real-request evaluation achieves average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) of 0.328/0.596 m on ORAD-3D and 0.266/0.526 m on RELLIS-3D, reducing FDE by 18.0% and 36.7% at request rates of 6.0% and 4.8%, respectively. These runs retain lower errors across four backbones and both datasets and reduce Qwen3-VL request-processing cost by factors of 16.6 and 20.8 under serial replay, while mechanism and motion-only controls identify persistent state correction as the main source of the observed accuracy benefit. The source code and evaluation materials are publicly available at this https URL .

AI.tldr: 越野驾驶的 VLA 模型需要频繁调用昂贵多模态推理,而简单复用旧预测又会让指令随车辆运动变化而失配。FastRoverVLA 用无需训练的接口把「视觉生成规划」与「运动条件化执行」解耦:在两次视觉预测之间维持被解码的计划,并用速度-曲率动作缓冲区吸收运动修正。作者报告在 3 s 时域下,真实请求评测的 FDE 分别降低 18.0%/36.7%,请求率仅为 6.0%/4.8%。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出:越野 VLA 模型能生成受场景条件的规划,但频繁的轨迹更新会反复调用昂贵得多模态推理;直接复用一次预测虽能降低开销,却使指令暴露于车辆运动变化之下,即「复用」与「运动变化」之间的错配。
AI.method: 输入是 VLA 模型解码出的计划(速度、曲率)与实测运动状态。方法是一个免训练接口:它不改变骨干网络、也不额外训练驾驶策略,而是在两次视觉预测之间保持已解码的计划;每次更新时,把速度-曲率动作缓冲区与实测运动对齐、合并进局部轨迹,再通过「消耗当前动作」把轨迹向前推进,并把修正后的剩余部分写回缓冲区,从而让运动修正跨更新累积保留。另有一条有界刷新规则,把新解码计划内的速度与曲率变化做归一化,并按由此得到的计划粗糙度分数分配短或长的复用预算。输出是被运动持续修正的执行轨迹,以及降低后的多模态请求频率。
AI.result: 3 s 时域、独立真实请求评测下,ORAD-3D 上 ADE/FDE 为 0.328/0.596 m,RELLIS-3D 上为 0.266/0.526 m,请求率分别为 6.0% 与 4.8% 时 FDE 降低 18.0% 与 36.7%。摘要另外称这些结果在四个骨干与两个数据集上均保持更低误差,并在串行重放下把 Qwen3-VL 的请求处理开销降低 16.6 倍与 20.8 倍;机制对照与仅运动对照表明,持续状态修正是精度收益的主要来源。摘要未报告 ADE 的改善幅度、对比基线的具体名称与数值、以及各骨干的单独数值。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能/世界模型方向,该工作展示了一条不重训模型即可延长 VLA 生成计划有效期的路径:把推理频率与执行频率解耦,用运动反馈维持计划一致性。证据边界是:所有数值均为作者自报,摘要只给出真实请求评测与串行重放开销,未说明实际车载硬件、闭环实车驾驶表现,也未给出统计显著性与完整基线对比。
AI.core_method: 在两次视觉预测之间用速度-曲率动作缓冲区对齐实测运动并写回修正后的剩余轨迹,配合按计划粗糙度分配短/长复用预算的有界刷新规则。

title: Stuck in Place: Stall Diagnosis and Remedies for JEPA Planners
summary: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models plan from pixels with model predictive control, yet often fail on tasks their model should handle. Test-time adaptation attributes such failures to model error under distribution shift and updates the weights on the current episode, without checking this attribution against the planning loop itself. We follow the executed planning loop on pushing tasks. In most settings, with and without distribution shift, nearly all failures (at least 96%) are stalls, where the object stays in place while the model predicts progress. The warm-started gradient-descent (GD) planner then returns nearly the same plan, a fixed point where the agent mostly idles. We propose Unstick, which pairs on-policy fine-tuning before deployment with a fixed-weight loop breaker: a residual memory of the episode's prediction errors or random re-initialization at every replan. With GD, Unstick recovers most of the adaptation gain on pushing tasks with the memory, and with re-initialization most of it on shape shifts but much less on visual shifts. A large part of what limits these planners under GD is thus a fixed point of the planning loop, present with and without distribution shift, which a planner with fixed weights can break. Code is available at this https URL .

AI.tldr: JEPA 世界模型用 MPC 从像素规划物体推动任务时经常失败，作者沿实际执行的规划循环检查，发现至少 96% 的失败是"物体不动而模型预测有进展"的停滞（stall），即热启动 GD 规划器回到近似同一计划的不动点。作者提出 Unstick：部署前的 on-policy 微调加固定权重的"回路打破器"（预测误差残差记忆或每次重规划随机重初始化）。
AI.motivation: 测试时自适应把此类失败归因于分布偏移下的模型误差并在当前回合更新权重，但没有把这个归因与规划循环本身对照验证。作者沿执行中的规划循环追踪，发现失败主要不是模型误差，而是规划循环的不动点：物体不动、模型却预测有进展。
AI.method: 输入是像素观测，JEPA 世界模型配合模型预测控制（MPC）生成动作计划。诊断阶段：在推物体任务上跟随实际执行的规划循环，检查失败时的计划与物体实际运动。干预阶段：Unstick 由两部分组成——部署前先做 on-policy 微调，再在推理时用固定权重（不更新模型权重）打破回路：要么在每次重规划时保留本回合预测误差的残差记忆，要么在每次重规划时随机重新初始化计划。输出是避免热启动 GD 回归同一计划、从而减少空转（idle）的规划行为。相对基线是仅在当前回合更新权重的测试时自适应。
AI.result: 摘要报告的核心定量结果是：在大多数设置下，无论有无分布偏移，至少 96% 的失败是 stall。Unstick 的增益为定性描述：在 GD 下，使用残差记忆可在推物体任务上恢复大部分自适应增益；使用重初始化可在形状偏移（shape shifts）上恢复大部分，但在视觉偏移（visual shifts）上恢复得少得多。摘要未报告具体的成功率数值、单位、样本量或统计检验，也未说明结果来自仿真还是真机。
AI.conclusion: 对 JEPA/世界模型规划而言，该工作指出至少一部分失败来自规划循环的不动点而非分布偏移下的模型误差，且这种不动点在有、无分布偏移时都出现，可用固定权重的规划器干预来打破。证据边界：诊断与修复均只在 pushing 任务的摘要描述范围内报告，缺少数值化的恢复率、仿真/真机条件与基线对比，因此不能推断该方法在其他任务或真实机器人上的效果。
AI.core_method: 先用执行中的规划循环诊断失败为停滞，再用"部署前 on-policy 微调 + 固定权重的误差记忆或每次重规划随机重初始化"打破规划器的不动点。

title: ACE-Brain-0.7: Learning Execution-Grounded Reasoning for Embodied Agents
summary: Reliable reasoning for long-horizon embodied tasks requires predictions grounded in the observed execution state. We present ACE-Brain-0.7, a 9B vision--language model that combines spatial grounding, task understanding, and progress estimation. To train the model, we curate 3.7 million question--answer pairs, drawing execution supervision from egocentric human videos, robot episodes, and simulation. These questions span different stages of an execution and connect task-level judgments with observed progress and outcomes. We then fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B on this collection together with additional task, spatial-grounding, and progress-estimation data. Across six public task-reasoning benchmarks, ACE-Brain-0.7 achieves an average score of 76.5, ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 72.7 and Claude Opus 5.5 at 73.5. Our model also leads the evaluated models in spatial grounding, averaging 75.90 across seven benchmarks and reaching 91.25 Acc@0.5 on RefCOCOg. Controlled evaluations further indicate that our task-only model makes more effective use of visual history and more accurately distinguishes execution states. Together, these results show that ACE-Brain-0.7 effectively combines spatial perception with temporal understanding, delivering strong execution-grounded reasoning and comparing favorably with closed-source models.

AI.tldr: ACE-Brain-0.7 是一个 9B 视觉-语言模型，用 370 万条来自自我中心人类视频、机器人回合与仿真的问答对微调 Qwen3.5-9B，把空间定位、任务理解与进度估计结合成"执行状态接地"的推理。作者报告其在六个公开任务推理基准上平均 76.5，高于 GPT-6 Astra 的 72.7 与 Claude Opus 5.5 的 73.5，并在空间定位上平均 75.90。
AI.motivation: 作者提出的问题是：长时程具身任务的可靠推理需要"以观测到的执行状态为依据"的预测，而现有模型未必把任务级判断与观察到的进度和结果连接起来。摘要未具体说明失败案例或现有方法的量化缺陷。
AI.method: 输入是执行过程的观测（自我中心人类视频、机器人回合、仿真）与问题；作者据此构建 370 万条问答对，问题覆盖执行的不同阶段，把任务级判断与观测到的进度、结果连接起来，并另加任务、空间定位、进度估计数据。方法上的改变是在 Qwen3.5-9B 上做微调，得到同时输出空间定位、任务理解与进度估计的 9B 模型。输出是执行接地的推理判断（含空间指代定位与任务/进度状态判别）。摘要未报告训练算力、上下文长度或推理开销。
AI.result: 作者报告：六个公开任务推理基准平均 76.5，高于 GPT-6 Astra 72.7 与 Claude Opus 5.5 73.5（分数单位，摘要未说明归一化方式）；空间定位在七个基准上平均 75.90，RefCOCOg 上 Acc@0.5 达 91.25，并称在被评测模型中领先（未给出各基线数值）。受控评测显示"仅任务"版本更有效利用视觉历史、更准确区分执行状态（摘要未给数值）。均为作者自报，未经独立验证；摘要未说明是仿真还是真机评测。

title: Demonstration-Free Skill Composition for Navigation and Manipulation
comment: 10 pages. Accepted at the Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation (ACRA 2026). Project page: this https URL
summary: Hierarchical reinforcement learning enables sequential tasks to be represented as compositions of separately trained skills. This paper evaluates demonstration-free hierarchical pipelines for MiniGrid navigation and robotic manipulation, comparing their training requirements and task performance with flat reinforcement learning baselines. The evaluation concerns complete pipelines with task-specific observation, reward and control structures. In navigation, two parameterised skills are reused across unseen FourRooms layouts under manually specified high-level plans. In manipulation, reaching, grasp alignment and lifting are trained separately, with downstream skills initialised from states collected during predecessor rollouts. Across unseen navigation layouts, the hierarchical pipeline substantially outperforms the evaluated flat DQN baselines while requiring fewer training interactions. In manipulation, the hierarchical chain requires fewer training steps than flat SAC and exhibits lower observed variation across seeds. The frozen Pick and Lift skills are further reused for stacking by training an additional Place skill.

AI.tldr: 论文评测无需演示数据的分层强化学习流水线：导航与操作任务中分别独立训练技能再组合，作者报告其表现优于或训练需求低于扁平 DQN/SAC 基线，但摘要未给出任何数值。
AI.motivation: 分层强化学习可将顺序任务表示为独立训练技能的组合，但在包含任务特定观测、奖励与控制结构的完整流水线中，无演示数据的分层方案相比扁平强化学习基线在训练需求与任务表现上的差异，本文认为需要评测。
AI.method: 输入是任务特定的观测、奖励与控制结构，不使用演示数据。导航侧：训练两个参数化技能，在人工指定的高层计划下复用到未见过的 FourRooms 布局。操作侧：到达、抓取对齐、举升三项技能分开训练，下游技能用前驱技能 rollout 中收集的状态初始化。输出是与扁平强化学习基线对照的完整分层流水线。
AI.result: 作者报告：在未见过的导航布局上，分层流水线大幅优于所评测的扁平 DQN 基线且所需训练交互更少；操作中分层链比扁平 SAC 所需训练步数更少，且跨种子观测到的波动更低。摘要未报告成功率、步数、交互次数等任何数值或统计检验，因此这些属于作者主张而非可核验的量化结果。

title: Spatially Conditioned Trajectory Diffusion
summary: Multi-Robot Motion Planning (MRMP) requires trajectories that avoid environmental obstacles and collisions between robots in a shared workspace. Diffusion-based planners often address obstacle avoidance through sampling-time guidance, while some conditioned approaches aggregate map geometry into a global representation. We present Spatially Conditioned Trajectory Diffusion (SCTD), a map-conditioned trajectory generator for multi-robot planning. SCTD retains multiple position-aware occupancy tokens accessed through cross-attention throughout a temporal U-Net, with hard endpoint inpainting enforcing start and goal states. One model trained on single-robot demonstrations across procedural environments generates obstacle-aware trajectories without sampling-time obstacle-cost guidance. High-level Conflict-Based Search (CBS) coordinates these trajectories through constrained replanning, retaining inter-agent guidance during sampling and reusing the model across workspace layouts and team sizes. Experiments assess single-robot success and trajectory quality, generalization to unfamiliar layouts with added obstacles, and coordinated multi-robot planning. On 15,000 held-out tasks, SCTD achieves higher success than the evaluated guided diffusion baseline, with the largest gains on hard-detour tasks, while trajectory-quality comparisons show smoother trajectories. Conditioning ablations show higher success with spatial tokens than with a global map embedding, and map-replacement tests demonstrate dependence on the supplied geometry. The resulting multi-robot system achieves higher team success than the compared diffusion baselines, with experiments covering teams of up to 15 robots.

title: Agentic Scaling of Embodied Tasks in Simulation for Synthetic Data Collection and Policy Evaluation

summary: Scaling embodied interaction data requires a broad collection of usable tasks, yet specifying and validating each task instance remains costly. We present AgenticTask, an agent-based framework that expands existing task collections under human intent. Its central representation links interaction requirements to object and part bindings, scene and robot configurations, initial conditions, and completion criteria. A task-generation agent reuses interaction structure to construct supported variations and revises incompatible configurations using validation feedback. A task-execution agent uses the same bindings and geometric records to select robot-supported skills and check completion against the original task criteria. On RoboCasa, the framework builds the AgenticTask collection, saving 16,450 task instances from 20,323 construction attempts at a throughput of 166.97 saved instances per elapsed hour, with 62.26% of construction attempts passing the configured physical checks. The execution agent completes approximately 38% of evaluated tasks, with successful cases spanning object placement, articulated manipulation, and sequential arrangement. Diagnostic analysis identifies improvement priorities in construction reliability, action selection, task-robot compatibility, and runtime integration. Together, these results demonstrate task-collection expansion with measured construction productivity and concrete execution evidence, providing a foundation for subsequent interaction-data collection for embodied AI.

title: Close&Safe: Maximal Task Preservation for Redundant Manipulators via C-Space Boundary Detour
summary: Contact-rich manipulation such as wiping, polishing and surface inspection specifies the task as a continuous end-effector trajectory rather than a goal pose. When an obstacle absent from the planning model intersects it, conventional planners return a collision-free path that may differ from the nominal throughout, discarding trajectory that was never obstructed. We present Close&Safe (Close to the intended task, Safe from obstacles), which decouples tracking from avoidance: the nominal is followed exactly wherever it remains feasible, and avoidance acts only on the interval where it is not, so tracking is hindered as little as the obstacle allows. On that interval we sample the configuration-space obstacle boundary within a corridor around the nominal, connect the samples into a roadmap, and search it for the detour that deviates least before rejoining the nominal at the earliest feasible configuration. We evaluate across diverse simulated obstacle configurations, physical Franka experiments, and ablations of key algorithmic components. The results demonstrate collision-free trajectory repair with localized task modification, while recovering 52.4-78% in simulation and on hardware.

AI.tldr: 针对接触式操作（擦拭、抛光、表面检测）中规划模型外障碍与标称末端轨迹相交、导致常规规划器丢弃整段未被阻挡轨迹的问题，Close&Safe 将跟踪与避障解耦：标称在可行处原样跟随，只在不可行区间内做局部绕行。作者报告在仿真与硬件上实现无碰撞轨迹修复并恢复 52.4-78%。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，接触式操作把任务规定为连续末端执行器轨迹而非目标位姿。当规划模型中不存在的障碍与该轨迹相交时，常规规划器返回一条可能全程偏离标称的无碰撞路径，从而丢弃那些从未被阻挡的轨迹段，造成不必要的任务退化。
AI.method: 输入是任务给定的标称末端轨迹，以及一个未出现在规划模型中的障碍。方法不重规划整条轨迹，而是解耦跟踪与避障：凡标称仍然可行的部分严格按标称执行，避障只作用在不可行的那个区间上。在该区间内，方法围绕标称取一条走廊，对走廊内的构型空间（C-space）障碍边界采样，将样本连成 roadmap，并在其上搜索“偏离最小、且在最早可行的构型处重新接回标称”的绕行路径。输出是一条无碰撞且修改局限在该区间的修复轨迹。相对基线：摘要只说“conventional planners”会返回一条与标称可能全程不同的无碰撞路径，未给出其具体实现细节。

AI.conclusion: 该工作把“接触式操作的轨迹修复”表述为只在不可行区间内做局部绕行的问题，并给出 C-space 障碍边界采样加 roadmap 搜索的实现机制；对具身智能的意义在于把避障代价限制在必要区间，从而尽量保留任务本身的轨迹语义，而不是让整条任务轨迹被重新规划。证据边界：本分析仅基于标题与摘要，未读全文；恢复比例的具体含义、基线对比、真实实验条件与效率数据均未在摘要中出现，所有结果均为作者自报，未经独立验证。

title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning

summary: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos. Across navigation and robotic manipulation, O$^{2}$LaF sets a new state of the art in few-shot action probing and enables stronger zero-shot action transfer across visual contexts and embodiments. Beyond generative video priors, we further extend our framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance. Our findings suggest a broader paradigm for latent-action learning: repurposing pretrained video models to discover transferable actions and predict their consequences.

title: TwoPass: Draft-Guided Few-Step Video Prediction for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Action-conditioned video prediction lets robots anticipate the visual consequences of their actions for planning and policy evaluation. Existing predictors denoise each future from noise without using their own estimate of it, which limits the quality of the predicted future, in particular of the manipulated objects, and requires many network calls. We present TwoPass, a self-conditioned training-and-inference framework that keeps the standard flow-matching objective. Self-Generated Draft Training supplies a detached clean-video estimate from the shared network as conditioning at the same noisy state. A Refinement-Only Late Adapter applies a dedicated residual transformation when a draft is present. At inference, Draft-Reuse Iterative Refinement obtains both a solver update and the next draft from each velocity prediction, requiring as few as 4 function evaluations (NFE) per video chunk. Training samples discrete solver-query noise levels and updates the pretrained backbone. Extensive experiments on Bridge and Language Table show that TwoPass achieves state-of-the-art results with 4 NFE, far fewer than the 50-59 calls of existing predictors. Code: this https URL .

title: Physical Laws without Physics Loss? Probing Learned Dynamics in Video World Models through Forced Response
summary: Do video world models learn physical laws without a physics loss, or merely imitate motion? Overall motion and appearance scores cannot settle it. We investigate this through nonlinear forced response: an excitation shakes the support of a suspended object. We introduce dual visual-numeric conditioning and adapt six image-to-video backbones to predict this motion using only the flow-matching loss. Wan predicts motion accurately and generalizes to unseen excitations, objects, poses, and scenes. Counterfactual tests suggest capabilities beyond replaying training videos. But what laws have they learned? We design three tiers of tests using Taylor expansions of the dynamics and geometry. All six reproduce the linear response, including resonance; five capture higher-order dynamics, including nonlinear softening. Remarkably, softening is barely present in training: only 0.74% of the swing's squared displacement. Extensions to a double pendulum and a rocking block show sustained dynamics are learned more faithfully than brief impacts. Yet learned dynamics may fail to appear when state estimation or propagation goes wrong. We turn these tests and findings into strategies to improve video training and generation.

title: Planning to Stop: Factored Certification and Terminal Repair for Noncircular Robots
summary: Tight-space navigation requires a robot to clear obstacles and stop inside its goal despite uncertainty. We present GeoDiff, a motion-program planner coupling original-goal stopped-set inclusion, witness-guided terminal repair, and factored proof compilation. An exact feasible-translation characterization guides repair; request-local reuse reduces repeated geometric work. We establish conditions for compiler equivalence and reach-and-stop soundness. Across 11,440 floorplan-derived jobs, GeoDiff certifies 61/139 tasks at 5-cm tolerance within 15 s, versus 44/139 for the stop-set baseline. The strongest observed external certificate adapter certifies 13/139 tasks from 119/139 native routes, separating route availability from certification. On tasks derived from public BARN maps, GeoDiff certifies 202/270 at 5-cm tolerance for a Jackal-shaped body, versus 3/270 for the portal baseline. Development analyses distinguish emitter savings from solver coverage, and 1,420 route-tracking episodes characterize the execution interface. These results show how terminal reasoning and proof reuse increase finite-budget certification coverage while preserving the original physical task and goal.

title: Hierarchical Spatiotemporal World Modeling with Content-Adaptive Spatial Addressing
summary: Long-horizon world modeling in partially observable environments requires compact memories that preserve spatial structure despite accumulated localization drift. Inspired by hippocampal episodic and spatial memory and the multi-periodic coding of entorhinal grid cells, we propose HiSTFormer, a hierarchical spatiotemporal world model, which adopts a layer-wise organization of local temporal RoPE and multi-periodic spatial RoPE, together with content-conditioned address offsets, to capture recent temporal context and long-range spatial structure. A fixed-capacity memory keeps KV storage and per-step attention cost bounded as the sequence grows. On MemoryMaze and HM3D, HiSTFormer outperforms strong world-model baselines within the training sequence length and generalizes substantially better to prediction horizons far beyond those seen during training, while using a compact model. The hierarchical spatiotemporal design remains effective across deeper Transformer stacks, with consistent gains as depth increases. These results show that hierarchical spatiotemporal organization and content-adaptive spatial addressing provide effective inductive biases for efficient long-horizon world modeling.

AI.tldr: 针对部分可观测环境中的长程世界建模与定位漂移问题，HiSTFormer 用分层时空 RoPE 和内容自适应空间地址偏移构建固定容量记忆；作者报告其在 MemoryMaze 与 HM3D 上优于强基线，并对远超训练视野的预测泛化更好，但摘要未给出数值。

title: Plan4D: Generative Plannable 4D Worlds

summary: Most world models for future prediction prioritize aestetic quality of generated videos, but offer only weak physical grounding and limited geometric consistency over time, due to the lack of explicit 4D modeling. Since training data with paired actions and dense 4D annotations is inherently scarce, plan4d leverages the complementary priors of foundational video generators and 3D reconstructors. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that plan4d achieves state-of-the-art performance in generative 4D modeling of environmental reactions. title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
summary: Artificial Spiking Neural Networks have gained remarkable attention in the last few years due to their proven ability in simulating biological neural cultures and producing similar activity and trends. Nevertheless, whether they can be trained for humanoid locomotion while retaining biological plausibility and robust performance at once remains an open question. We study this problem by proposing a biologically inspired spiking network, trained by different learning schemes and tested on the H1-2 Unitree Humanoid. These schemes differ in how recurrent weights are trained. Ordered from most to least biologically faithful, they are: a fixed reservoir mimicking an in-vitro neural culture, where recurrent weights are kept frozen and only a linear readout is trained, the same network but with its synapses trained by reward-modulated spike timing dependent plasticity and eligibility propagation, and finally backpropagation through time as a non biological baseline for comparison. All schemes relied on distillation of a reinforcement learning expert policy with dataset aggregation. We show that e-prop reached 100% survival rate matching backpropagation through time, whereas both the fixed reservoir and the reward-modulated STDP, though the closest to biological cultures, plateaued at a much lower performance (~43.7% and ~11% survival). We explore in further detail which trends a real culture could and could not produce until now. Finally we demonstrate brief bipedal stepping on a full size humanoid H1-2.

title: TuringPAI: A Foundation for On-Device Physical AI
summary: Physical AI requires models that understand spatial relationships and dynamic environments and translate observations into actions under limited onboard compute. We present TuringPAI, a family of models for on-device Physical AI comprising TuringPAI-VL for shared vision-language understanding, TuringPAI-Drive for autonomous driving, and TuringPAI-Embodied for robotic manipulation. TuringPAI-VL is a 0.65B model built on HybridViT-MLQ, which combines convolutional local aggregation with Transformer-based global modeling. Multi-scale Latent Queries integrate spatial features and observation history within the same visual Transformer, providing a compact, structured interface to the language model. Training combines general vision-language data with geometric, cross-view, and temporal supervision. TuringPAI-VL supports general multimodal understanding and improves quantitative geometric perception over Qwen2-VL-2B, while providing a shared initialization for the two downstream VLA models. For autonomous driving, TuringPAI-Drive maintains all evaluated ADE/FDE metrics within 1.2\% of a full-token HybridViT baseline using the MLQ interface and achieves comparable aggregate scores in an in-house simulation evaluation. Using XPeng Native Runtime (XNRT) on a single NVIDIA Orin-X SoC, TuringPAI-Drive generates trajectories at 12\,Hz in on-vehicle operation. For robotic manipulation, TuringPAI-Embodied achieves a 96.8\% average success rate across the four LIBERO suites. These results demonstrate a shared vision-language foundation for driving and robotic manipulation under practical on-device constraints.

title: MixReact: Physics-Based Reactive Humanoid Control from Multimodal Cues via a Discrete-Continuous Mixture of Transformers
summary: Humanoid agents in everyday environments are expected to react to diverse cues as humans do, with semantically appropriate and physically executable behaviors. Existing cue-driven reaction generation methods support only a narrow range of cue modalities and are limited to purely kinematic generation, leaving the resulting reactions susceptible to physical artifacts. To this end, we present MixReact, the first unified framework for physics-based reactive humanoid control from text, audio, and video cues, integrating a Discrete--Continuous Mixture of Transformers (DisCo-MoT) for state prediction with a History-aware Action Transformer (HAT) for physical execution. DisCo-MoT couples a discrete masked-modeling branch with a continuous autoregressive diffusion branch via one-way mixture attention within a MoT architecture. Guidance from discrete context mitigates collapse into averaged behaviors in one-to-many reaction generation, while direct prediction in continuous state space bypasses the decoding bottleneck of discrete representations. HAT then maps the predicted next state and observed execution history to executable actions, enabling robust closed-loop control in physics-based simulation. Experiments across all three modalities demonstrate consistent improvements over the baselines in fidelity, diversity, and physical consistency, while ablations validate the complementary contributions of the components. title: SteerTrace: Tracing How Target Attacks Steer World Action Models
summary: World action models (WAMs) predict future videos and actions with one backbone, and their imagined future is often seen as a safety signal. We introduce SteerTrace, a targeted universal attack on WAMs that also traces its effect inside the model. One $\ell_\infty$-bounded (4/255) perturbation per model, shared across frames, tasks, and camera views, pushes the executed action toward an attacker-chosen target. On eight WAMs from four families (FastWAM, Faster-WAM, OpenWAM and LingBot-VA) on LIBERO and RoboTwin, it drives task success close to zero and moves the attacked action toward the target. Same-budget noise and BadWAM produce little action shift in the target direction. We use the signed targeted effect to measure how much of the effect each intervention removes or reproduces. Under the standard attack, restoring future tokens removes 61-94% of the targeted effect in the five models whose action experts attend to them. When the attack is constrained to keep the predicted future close to the clean prediction, the targeted effect can become more dependent on current-frame tokens. In three of these five models, restoring current-frame tokens removes 87-99% of the effect, compared with 9-15% for future tokens. In six models, restoring just 0.36% of the FFN neurons in layers 10-29 of the video expert removes 72-96% of the targeted effect. Residual directions 2-16 hold only 11-18% of the shift energy, yet removing them cancels most of the targeted effect.

AI.tldr: SteerTrace 是针对世界动作模型（WAM）的定向通用攻击：每个模型只优化一个 ℓ∞ 上界为 4/255、跨帧/任务/相机视角共享的扰动，就能把执行动作推向攻击者指定目标并把任务成功率压到接近零；作者同时用"恢复/移除某类内部表示"的干预来追踪该定向效果来自模型何处。
AI.motivation: WAM 用同一个骨干同时预测未来视频与动作，其"想象出的未来"常被当作安全信号；该摘要的出发点是检验这一信号能否被定向操纵，以及攻击效果在模型内部依托哪些部分产生。
AI.method: 输入是观测帧与任务，方法为每个模型优化单个 ℓ∞ 有界（4/255）扰动，该扰动跨帧、任务和相机视角共享，目标是把执行动作推向攻击者选定的目标动作（定向、通用攻击，非随机破坏）。在此之上，作者用"有符号的定向效果"作为量度：通过把未来 token、当前帧 token、视频专家 FFN 神经元、残差方向等内部表示恢复或移除，测量每种干预能消除或复现多少定向效果，从而定位效果来源。输出是攻击后的动作（被推向目标）以及各内部构件对定向效果的贡献比例。摘要未报告优化算法、迭代次数、模型规模或计算开销。
AI.result: 在 LIBERO 与 RoboTwin 的 8 个 WAM（FastWAM、Faster-WAM、OpenWAM、LingBot-VA 四族）上，攻击使任务成功率接近 0 并推动动作趋向目标；同预算噪声与 BadWAM 在目标方向上的动作位移很小。标准攻击下，在动作专家关注未来 token 的 5 个模型中，恢复未来 token 消除 61–94% 的定向效果。当把攻击约束为保持预测未来接近干净预测时，效果更依赖当前帧 token：这 5 个模型中的 3 个里，恢复当前帧 token 消除 87–99%，而恢复未来 token 只消除 9–15%。6 个模型中，仅恢复视频专家第 10–29 层中 0.36% 的 FFN 神经元即消除 72–96% 的定向效果；残差方向 2–16 只占 11–18% 的位移能量，移除它们却能抵消大部分定向效果。上述均为作者自报结果，摘要未报告真机/仿真区分、统计显著性或完整基线细节。

title: Improving Imitation Policies for Multi-Phase Tasks through Residual Learning Allocation
summary: Residual reinforcement learning corrects an imitation-trained base policy using a limited budget of environment interaction. In a task with several phases, this budget must be divided among the phases, and the phase in which the base policy fails is not necessarily the phase in which a correction most improves task completion. We formalize this distinction through the completion gain: the change in full-task completion probability when, during a single phase, a state-feedback controller replaces selected components of the base policy's action. We decompose the completion gain into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase, and we estimate it from paired episodes. The positive estimates determine which action components the residual policy corrects and how training episodes are distributed across phases. In stochastic point-mass docking experiments, most failures occurred in the final docking phase, whereas the largest completion gain occurred in the preceding channel phase; gain-based allocation improved completion over allocation proportional to failure counts and, in a variant with a longer approach, over uniform allocation at half of the budget. In simulated bimanual robotic assembly, the completion-gain estimates were positive only for insertion and release, although few failures occurred during release; in a second assembly configuration, a residual policy trained in the release phase improved completion from held-out states at the start of release by 16.9%.

AI.tldr: 该工作针对多阶段任务中残差强化学习交互预算难以分配的问题，提出 completion gain 并据此选择残差修正的动作分量与各阶段训练回合分配。点质量对接与双臂装配实验中，增益最大的阶段未必是失败最多的阶段；按增益分配在部分设定下优于按失败比例或均匀分配，一个装配配置中释放阶段残差策略将完成率提升 16.9%。

title: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence
summary: World models are increasingly used to simulate physical interactions, but training a separate model for each environment limits scalability. Cross-environment prediction requires identifying the current physical rule, which appearance alone may not reveal. We therefore study visual calibration: using object motion and interactions in a short video as direct evidence to infer the current rule and predict motion under that rule from a different initial state. However, differences in data availability across physical conditions can yield a long-tailed training distribution, biasing models toward common rules even when evidence supports rare ones. To study this challenge, we introduce TailWorld, which evaluates the transfer of demonstrated rules across initial states while independently controlling training imbalance and calibration informativeness. The benchmark compares predictions with two reference futures from the same prediction initial state, one following the demonstrated rule and the other a common rule, to measure prediction bias toward common dynamics. We further propose Rule Inference for Transfer (RIFT), which learns how different rules affect object motion, infers the current rule from calibration interactions, and applies it to prediction from a new initial state. RIFT explicitly controls the influence of training frequency on rule inference, allowing sufficiently informative observational evidence to support rare rules. Experiments on TailWorld show that RIFT improves prediction accuracy and physical consistency across varying training imbalances and distribution shifts, with gains in predicting rare dynamics.

AI.motivation: 为每个环境单独训练世界模型限制可扩展性；而跨环境预测需要先识别当前物理规则，外观本身可能无法揭示该规则。作者进一步指出，不同物理条件的数据可得性差异会形成长尾训练分布，使模型在证据支持稀有规则时仍偏向常见规则。
AI.method: 输入是一段短视频中的物体运动与交互（作为“视觉校准”证据），以及一个用于预测的新初始状态。方法（RIFT，Rule Inference for Transfer）学习不同规则如何影响物体运动，从校准交互中推断当前规则，并把该规则应用到新初始状态下的运动预测；相对基线，它显式控制训练频率对规则推断的影响，使信息量足够的观测证据能够支持稀有规则。输出是遵循所推断规则的未来运动预测。TailWorld 则是一个基准：在独立控制训练不平衡程度与校准信息量的同时，评测已演示规则向新初始状态的迁移，并用来自同一预测初始状态的两条参考未来（一条遵循演示规则、一条遵循常见规则）衡量预测偏向常见动力学的程度。

title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
summary: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement reuses it to improve perceptual quality, while three-step refinement strengthens camera following and trajectory consistency. These findings motivate transition-aware refinement. On WBench Navigation, SpecWM improves visual quality at 1.63$\times$ speedup over the target and raises NavScore from the draft's 75.99 to 85.63, achieving the best quality-speed-control trade-off. Additionally, our LongSpecBench shows sustained quality and control over long, multi-turn rollouts, while experiments on Hy-Nomas validate SpecWM across backbones and denoising budgets.

AI.tldr: SpecWM 针对流式视频世界模型提出免训练推理框架：用目标模型的隐空间速度场验证草稿块，并把验证信号复用为纠正量，以两个阈值选择接受、精炼或拒绝。作者报告在 WBench Navigation 上以相对目标模型 1.63× 加速改善视觉质量，NavScore 从草稿的 75.99 提升到 85.63。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，已有投机式方法依赖对已解码帧的外部评分器做验证：验证只覆盖外部评分器的评价维度，还引入解码与评分开销；且这些分数不提供纠正，草稿被拒后仍需昂贵的目标模型重生成。
AI.method: 输入是流式世界模型生成的草稿块（chunk）及其目标模型信息。SpecWM 不训练模型，而是改用目标模型的隐空间速度场来验证草稿块；验证过程同时产生可复用的纠正量，再用两个阈值把每个草稿块分到 Accept、Refine、Reject。一步精炼复用该纠正量提升感知质量，三步精炼加强相机跟随与轨迹一致性，由此引出 transition-aware refinement。相对摘要所述的基线，变化在于把“解码帧上的外部奖励验证”换成“目标隐空间速度场验证 + 验证即纠正”，以减少仅拒绝后重生成的需求。

key_results.setting: LongSpecBench，长时多轮 rollout；具体指标、数值、基线与条件摘要未报告。

title: Beyond Easy Clients: Difficulty- and Improvement-Aware Aggregation for Federated Reinforcement Learning in Robot Navigation
summary: Federated reinforcement learning enables a fleet of robots to jointly learn a shared navigation policy without exchanging raw experience. In practice, however, the robots rarely operate in the same conditions: an open aisle is far easier to navigate than a cluttered room, and takes less learning to master. Standard federated aggregation rules ignore this. Uniform averaging weights every client equally, whether or not it is still learning, and weighting by episode return is worse, since easy environments permit high returns by construction. Both failures stem from what we call the \emph{plateau problem}: once a client masters its environment, its updates carry little new information even though its reported return remains high. We propose \emph{FedDIA}, which scores each client by how much its local training improves the global model it received, amplified by the difficulty of its environment. Difficulty is inferred from the model's own performance, without requiring any description of the environment. Both signals are measured against the global model, so they are comparable across clients. On a mapless navigation task with eight heterogeneous clients, FedDIA reaches a mean success rate of $75.5\%$ across training and held-out environments, against $68.7\%$ for the strongest federated baseline. Its advantage holds when the models are transferred to hand-authored warehouse and living-space layouts, or when one of the clients is defective.

AI.tldr: 联邦强化学习让机器人车队共享导航策略，但客户端环境难度不一，均匀平均与按回报加权都因"平台期问题"失效。FedDIA 按客户端对全局模型的改进量打分并用环境难度放大，在八客户端无地图导航任务上把平均成功率做到 75.5%（最强联邦基线 68.7%）。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，车队中的机器人很少处于相同条件：开放走廊远比杂乱房间好导航，也更快学会。标准联邦聚合规则忽略这一点——均匀平均对所有客户端一视同仁，不管它是否还在学习；按 episode return 加权更糟，因为简单环境本身就允许高回报。作者把这两类失败归因于"平台期问题"：客户端一旦掌握其环境，其更新即使回报仍然很高，携带的新信息也很少。
AI.method: 输入是各客户端在本地训练后得到的更新，以及它收到的全局模型；方法不依赖任何环境描述。FedDIA 给每个客户端打两个分数：一是它的本地训练相对所收到全局模型的改进量，二是该环境的难度（由模型自身表现推断得到）。两者都以全局模型为参照测量，因而可在客户端之间比较，再据此加权聚合出新的全局导航策略。相对于均匀平均和按回报加权这两类被指出的基线聚合规则，改变的是权重来源：由"是否还在带来改进"和"环境有多难"共同决定。
AI.result: 作者报告，在八异构客户端的无地图（mapless）导航任务上，FedDIA 在训练环境与留出环境上的平均成功率为 75.5%，最强联邦基线为 68.7%；二者同为成功率数值，因此差异属于百分点而非相对百分比提升（摘要未给出具体百分点差）。摘要还称该优势在模型迁移到手写仓库与居住空间布局、或其中一个客户端失效时依然保持，但这些条件均未报告数值。摘要未报告统计显著性、客户端规模之外的样本量或硬件条件。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能中的多机器人协同学习，这篇工作提示：聚合权重应看"更新带来多少新信息"而非"当前表现多好"，并且难度可以从模型自身表现推断而无需环境标签。证据边界是：摘要只报告了无地图导航这一任务上的成功率数字，迁移与缺陷客户端部分只有定性陈述；摘要未说明实验是仿真还是真机，也未给出通信或计算开销，因此不能据此推断真实车队部署效果或效率优势。
AI.core_method: 用客户端本地训练对全局模型造成的改进量打分，再按由模型自身表现推断出的环境难度放大该分数，据此加权聚合联邦导航策略。

key_results.finding: FedDIA 在八客户端无地图导航任务上达到 75.5% 平均成功率（跨训练与留出环境），最强联邦基线为 68.7%；两者均为成功率数值，属百分点级差异，摘要未报告相对百分比提升。
key_results.setting: 无地图导航任务，八个异构客户端，指标为跨训练环境与留出环境的平均成功率；对照为最强联邦基线。摘要未报告仿真或真机、训练步数、硬件与统计显著性。
key_results.evidence_quote: On a mapless navigation task with eight heterogeneous clients, FedDIA reaches a mean success rate of $75.5\%$ across training and held-out environments, against $68.7\%$ for the strongest federated baseline.

key_results.finding: 作者称优势在模型迁移到手写仓库与居住空间布局、以及其中一个客户端失效时仍然保持；摘要未给出这些条件下的任何数值。
key_results.setting: 迁移到手写仓库布局与居住空间布局；以及一个客户端存在缺陷的场景。摘要未报告具体成功率、下降幅度或失效客户端的缺陷类型。
key_results.evidence_quote: Its advantage holds when the models are transferred to hand-authored warehouse and living-space layouts, or when one of the clients is defective.

limitations: 作者在摘要中未明确列出自身方法的局限性；所报告的失败模式是针对均匀平均与按回报加权这两类既有聚合规则的批评，而非对 FedDIA 的反面证据。
摘要未报告实验是仿真还是真实机器人部署，也未说明八客户端之外的规模、随机种子或统计显著性；这些是摘要未报告的信息，不代表方法缺乏相应能力。
迁移到仓库/居住空间布局以及客户端失效两种情形只有定性陈述，摘要未报告数值结果与对照条件。

title: From Sequence to Space: Explicit Spatial Belief with Vision-Language Distillation for Active Geo-Localization
summary: Active geo-localization (AGL) asks an agent to navigate a small aerial search grid and reach a target specified by an aerial image, a ground-level photograph, or text. Existing methods align the goal modalities well, but they keep the navigation state inside a large sequential Transformer and train with a dense distance reward that uses the hidden goal location. This paper proposes EAGLE, an Explicit spatial-belief Agent for Geo-Localization and Exploration. Offline training jointly optimizes a teacher-conditioned Swin branch and a context-free Swin student from the same randomly masked partial mosaics. The teacher branch attends to frozen full-scene context extracted by Qwen2.5-VL-7B, both branches receive masked-cell aerial-feature reconstruction and uncertainty supervision, while the student additionally distills stop-gradient feature predictions from the teacher. After distillation, Qwen, its cached context, and the teacher-attention branch are discarded. The retained student predicts cell-level aerial-feature embeddings and predictive uncertainty from partial observations alone. These predictions are combined with the modality-aligned goal embedding and a trajectory-derived visitation mask to construct the spatial belief tensor. The student is then frozen while a compact CNN actor-critic is optimized with PPO. EAGLE achieves state-of-the-art average success rates of 78.1%, 76.4%, and 76.8% on MASA, xBD zero-shot transfer, and the MM-GAG zero-shot aerial-goal split, respectively, without using a VLM or cached visual tokens at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

AI.tldr: 该文提出 EAGLE：把 Qwen2.5-VL-7B 提供的全场景上下文离线蒸馏进一个只依赖部分观测的 Swin 学生网络，使其能预测单元格级航拍特征嵌入与不确定性，从而显式构造空间信念张量。作者报告在 MASA、xBD 零样本迁移与 MM-GAG 零样本航拍目标划分上平均成功率为 78.1%、76.4%、76.8%，并称推理时不需要 VLM 或缓存视觉 token。
AI.motivation: 主动地理定位（AGL）要求智能体在小型航拍搜索网格中导航，并抵达由航拍图、地面照片或文本指定的目标。摘要指出，现有方法虽然能对齐目标模态，但把导航状态保存在大型序列 Transformer 内部，并用依赖隐藏目标位置的稠密距离奖励进行训练。
AI.method: 输入是随机掩码的部分航拍拼图（partial mosaics），并由此训练两条分支：教师条件 Swin 分支与无上下文的 Swin 学生。教师分支关注由 Qwen2.5-VL-7B 提取的冻结全场景上下文；两分支都接受被掩码单元格的航拍特征重建与不确定性监督，学生额外蒸馏教师停止梯度的特征预测。蒸馏后丢弃 Qwen、其缓存上下文与教师注意力分支。保留的学生仅从部分观测预测单元格级航拍特征嵌入与预测不确定性；这些预测与模态对齐的目标嵌入、轨迹导出的访问掩码结合，构成空间信念张量。随后冻结学生，用一个紧凑 CNN actor-critic 以 PPO 优化。相对于摘要所述基线，关键变化是把导航状态显式写成空间信念张量、并把大模型上下文离线蒸馏到轻量学生中；摘要未说明 EAGLE 在 RL 阶段使用何种奖励。
AI.result: 作者报告 EAGLE 在 MASA、xBD 零样本迁移、MM-GAG 零样本航拍目标划分上分别达到 78.1%、76.4%、76.8% 的平均成功率，并称其为 state-of-the-art；摘要未给出与具体基线的差值和对比条件。作者同时报告推理阶段不使用 VLM 或缓存视觉 token。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能/世界模型方向而言，该工作给出一种思路：用大视觉语言模型提供场景上下文作为离线监督，把知识压缩为可在线运行的部分观测空间信念预测器，从而在不背负 VLM 推理成本的情况下支持导航决策。证据边界是：摘要只报告三个基准的平均成功率与“SOTA”声明，没有真机实验、计算/延迟数字、与具体基线的数值对比、消融或统计显著性，因此不能推断实际部署可行性与相对提升幅度。
AI.core_method: 离线把冻结大 VLM 的全场景上下文蒸馏到只吃部分观测的 Swin 学生，使其直接预测单元格级航拍特征与不确定性，拼成空间信念张量供轻量 PPO 策略使用。

key_results.finding: 在 MASA、xBD 零样本迁移与 MM-GAG 零样本航拍目标划分上平均成功率分别为 78.1%、76.4%、76.8%，作者称之为 state-of-the-art（摘要未给具体基线数值）。
key_results.setting: 任务：主动地理定位（AGL）在航拍搜索网格中抵达目标；三个基准：MASA、xBD 零样本迁移、MM-GAG 零样本航拍目标划分；指标：平均成功率；基线：摘要称现有方法为对比对象但未报告其数值；真机/仿真条件摘要未报告。
key_results.evidence_quote: EAGLE achieves state-of-the-art average success rates of 78.1%, 76.4%, and 76.8% on MASA, xBD zero-shot transfer, and the MM-GAG zero-shot aerial-goal split, respectively, without using a VLM or cached visual tokens at inference.

key_results.finding: 推理阶段不使用 VLM，也不使用缓存视觉 token（摘要未给出延迟、显存或算力数值）。
key_results.setting: 推理阶段；模型规模与硬件条件摘要未报告；对比对象为使用 VLM/缓存视觉 token 的既有方法（未给具体名称与数值）。
key_results.evidence_quote: without using a VLM or cached visual tokens at inference

limitations: 作者自陈局限：摘要未报告任何作者明确陈述的局限性。
摘要未报告：与具体基线的数值对比、差值或提升幅度（仅称 state-of-the-art）；也未报告样本量、随机种子、统计显著性或消融结果。
摘要未报告：实验是仿真还是真机、硬件与推理延迟、以及 RL 阶段所用的奖励设计；代码仅称“将公开”，未给出可用链接。

title: Inhabitant: An Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Human-Scene Interaction with Spatial Control and Quantitative Feedback
summary: Recent work on human-scene interaction (HSI) generation moves from single interactions to long-horizon interaction, where a language-model agent plans and executes a sequence of interactions in a 3D scene under one instruction. However, existing agents struggle in challenging everyday scenarios (e.g., picking up a toy and throwing it into a basket) because they lack spatial control over the motion and quantitative feedback on its execution, and they often fail to complete the interaction sequence. To address these gaps, we present Inhabitant, a training-free agent framework in which the agent specifies each motion through positions, paths and poses, measures how the executed interaction deviates from its intent, and revises the control specification accordingly. For an extensive evaluation in such scenarios, we build Inhabit, a benchmark of 75 household tasks in 31 furniture layouts of an apartment, in which every task chains one to three goals on movable objects and is carried out by the whole body, excluding fingers. On Inhabit, Inhabitant completes 98.7\% of the tasks with Claude Opus 5.5, and 93.3\% and 82.7\% with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon, respectively. Ablations confirm that without spatial control the agent fails most tasks, and without quantitative feedback its motion becomes less precise. Code is available on the project page.

AI.tldr: Inhabitant 是一个免训练的语言模型智能体框架，用空间控制（位置/路径/姿态）加定量执行反馈来规划并修正长时程人–场景交互；作者在自建基准 Inhabit（75 个家务任务、31 种家具布局）上报告最高 98.7% 的任务完成率，并称去掉空间控制后多数任务失败。
AI.motivation: 既有长时程人–场景交互生成智能体在"捡起玩具并投进篮子"这类日常场景中表现不佳，原因是缺少对动作的空间控制、也缺少对执行结果的定量反馈，因而常常无法完成整条交互序列。作者据此提出补足这两点的智能体框架。
AI.method: 输入是单条语言指令与一个 3D 场景；智能体（调用现成语言模型，不做训练）把指令拆成长时程交互序列，并以位置、路径、姿态显式规定每一段动作，然后执行；执行后再度量实际交互与原始意图的偏差，据此修改控制规格并迭代，最终输出满足指令的整身交互序列（不含手指）。相对既有智能体，改动点是把"几何控制规格 + 执行偏差的定量反馈闭环"显式加入规划-执行流程。作者还构建了评测用基准 Inhabit。
AI.result: 在自建基准 Inhabit（75 个家务任务、31 种公寓家具布局，任务链 1–3 个可移动物体目标、由整身完成、不含手指）上，作者报告 Inhabitant 配合 Claude Opus 5.5 完成任务率 98.7%，配合 Claude Sonnet 5.5 为 93.3%，配合 Gemini 4 Argon 为 82.7%。消融显示：去掉空间控制后智能体在多数任务上失败；去掉定量反馈后其动作变得不够精确。摘要未给出与既有 HSI 智能体的数值对比，也未报告运行时间、成本或失败分布。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与长时程交互研究而言，该工作提示：在不训练模型的前提下，把动作的几何空间控制与执行偏差的定量反馈显式嵌入语言模型智能体的规划回路，可显著提升整身家务任务链的完成率，并说明"能否指定与校正空间细节"比单纯扩大模型规模更关键（作者报告的不同后端完成率差异与此一致）。证据边界：全部数值来自作者自建基准与三个语言模型后端，摘要未报告任何真实机器人实验，也未说明场景是仿真还是真实环境，因此不能推断真实部署效果。
AI.core_method: 语言模型智能体把每段交互显式写成位置、路径与姿态的可执行控制规格，并在执行后量化实际动作与意图的偏差、据此改写控制规格，全程不训练模型。

key_results.finding: 消融表明：没有空间控制时智能体在多数任务上失败；没有定量反馈时其动作精确度下降（摘要未给出具体指标数值）。
key_results.setting: 在与主实验相同的 Inhabit 基准上的消融实验，分别移除空间控制与定量反馈两个组件；摘要未报告消融的具体任务数、指标数值或统计信息。
key_results.evidence_quote: Ablations confirm that without spatial control the agent fails most tasks, and without quantitative feedback its motion becomes less precise.

title: DMT-Attack: Diffusion-Prior Texture Search for Closed-Loop Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely on visual feedback throughout manipulation, making them vulnerable to persistent texture attacks. However, optimized patterns can stand out from their surroundings, making an attack easier to notice and its carrier more likely to be inspected or removed. To address this limitation, our key insight is to search the structured image distribution of a diffusion model for natural-looking textures while using closed-loop feedback to identify task-disruptive candidates. Based on this idea, we propose DMT-Attack, a gradient-free gray-box attack that generates textures for ordinary scene objects such as tablecloths. A frozen text-conditioned diffusion model defines the search space, and an eight-expert latent proposal network is initialized from evaluated teacher latents and refined using rollout feedback. We evaluate DMT-Attack against pi_0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT across four LIBERO suites. DMT-Attack achieves a macro clean-conditioned attack success rate (cASR) of 57.9%, compared with 44.7% for UPA-RFAS and 19.7% for random natural textures. It also attains higher scene similarity and a lower clean-calibrated detector flag rate (45% versus 97.5-100% for optimized patch baselines). These results demonstrate that natural-looking textures can disrupt VLA visual feedback and closed-loop decision-making, motivating defenses that jointly assess visual appearance and task behavior.

title: PRIO: Pre-trained Representation for Interactive Objects in 4D Worlds
summary: 3D worlds can now be captured, reconstructed, and generated at scale, yet the objects in them stay still: a pressed pillow does not compress, and a pulled door does not swing. Bringing these objects into interactive 4D world models requires a representation of how they can move, deform, and respond physically to user actions in real time. We present PRIO, a pre-trained representation for interactive objects. Given static geometry, PRIO predicts an object-specific configuration space in a single forward pass. This space provides generalized coordinates for Lagrangian mechanics, allowing physical laws and user actions to govern motion. Configurations are linear in these coordinates, allowing the quantities needed by the dynamics to be precomputed. Dynamics then run at interactive rates without further network inference. Pre-trained on diverse 4D trajectories, PRIO learns priors over object configurations that generalize to unseen shapes. It supports meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussians, bringing objects in reconstructed and generated scenes into interaction. We demonstrate its use in real-to-sim workflows and robot manipulation. In addition, compared with existing 4D generation methods, PRIO generates dynamics faster and follows user actions more faithfully.

title: PAD: Policy-Aware Data Valuation for Autonomous Driving
summary: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. However, additional data do not guarantee better policies: a demonstration that benefits one planner may be redundant or harmful to another. Existing curation methods typically infer data value from intrinsic sample properties or training-dependent proxies that do not measure downstream policy utility. To address this, we introduce \textbf{Policy-Aware Data Valuation (PAD)}, a framework that assigns each candidate demonstration a utility specific to the target driving policy. PAD combines scene-level calibration feedback with projected policy gradients and a regularized approximation of local training geometry, producing scalable influence-based values for the policy. A controlled group-removal study establishes the directional fidelity of these values, while cross-planner analysis shows that the same candidate pool induces markedly different rankings across planner families. On DiffusionDrive, PAD improves EPDMS over real-only training by $3.5$ points on NavTest and $5.0$ points on NavHard. Policy-specific curation consistently outperforms real-only and full-pool training across diffusion-, regression-, and flow-matching-based planners while substantially reducing scene-level regressions. These results establish policy-aware data valuation as a basis for replacing indiscriminate data accumulation with targeted policy improvement, enabling more efficient and reliable scaling of autonomous-driving systems.

AI.tldr: 针对端到端自动驾驶中“数据增多不等于策略变好”的问题，PAD 为每条候选示教数据估计面向目标驾驶策略的效用值，并据此筛选数据。作者报告在 DiffusionDrive 上，EPDMS 相比仅用真实数据训练在 NavTest 提升 3.5 点、在 NavHard 提升 5.0 点。
AI.motivation: 端到端自动驾驶依赖扩大示教数据规模，但数据增长并不保证策略性能成比例提升；同一条示教对一个规划器有益，对另一个规划器可能冗余甚至有害。现有数据筛选方法通常依据样本内在属性或与训练相关的代理指标，无法衡量数据对下游策略的实际效用。

title: From Self-Play RL to Constrained Control: Distilling DiffMPC Students with DAgger
comment: 18 pages, 10 main content pages, 3 figures, L4DC submission
summary: Self-play reinforcement learning (RL) produces strong driving policies, but these policies are hard to verify or interpret. Differentiable model predictive control (DiffMPC) can enforce explicit constraints, but it is usually trained by imitating logged data or with costly RL. To add constraints to an already trained policy, we keep a PPO teacher's backbone and replace its action head with a DiffMPC that enforces road boundary half-planes and agent ellipses. We then distill the student with DAgger in the teacher's self-play simulator. Over 9 seeds, the constrained student of a smaller teacher matches its teacher on nuPlan and beats it on CARLA and on out-of-distribution Waymo scenes. For a stronger teacher, the student has fewer failures on nuPlan and Waymo, while staying level on CARLA. Its distillation takes no more than 30% of the teacher's training time.

title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation

summary: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. title: Mapping the Wind to Find the Source: Online Physics-Informed Gas Source Localization with Mobile Robots
summary: Gas Source Localization (GSL) with mobile robots is challenging because wind and gas measurements are spatially sparse, noisy, and potentially affected by robot motion. Indoor airflow can vary substantially across space, while detailed environmental layouts, boundary conditions, or precomputed airflow fields are often unavailable. Moreover, hazardous sources must be localized as quickly as possible, making exhaustive exploration impractical. This paper presents a lightweight physics-informed probabilistic framework for efficient GSL under spatially varying indoor airflow. As the robot navigates, it continuously collects wind and gas measurements and reconstructs the spatially varying airflow field online. The estimated wind field drives a forward dispersion model that predicts the gas pattern for each candidate source location. These predictions are compared with the measured gas pattern to update a probabilistic belief over the source location. As the wind field is reconstructed incrementally, the framework also accounts for the spatially non-uniform reliability of wind field estimation and its influence on the source estimation. The resulting belief map is then used for informative path planning to guide the robot toward informative regions. High-fidelity simulations provide a comprehensive evaluation of the individual components and their integrations within the complete system, while physical indoor experiments assess the system performance under realistic sensing, motion, and airflow conditions. The results demonstrate that incorporating lightweight physical knowledge significantly improves localization robustness under spatially complex airflow and enables more efficient exploration.

title: Dynamic Human-Robot Role Allocation through Entropy-Based Monitoring and LLM Reasoning
summary: Role allocation strategies in human-robot collaboration typically assign tasks to both the human and the robot, limiting the user's ability to take initiative. Furthermore, allocation decisions may conflict with the user's intentions, and the rationale behind such allocations may remain unclear, potentially reducing both acceptance and collaboration fluency. The novelty of the proposed framework is that the human is left free to contribute to the task, while the robot is dynamically allocated activities through a cost-driven Behavior Tree architecture according to user-expressed preferences and behavior. Explicit preferences are extracted from natural language instructions using a large language model, whereas human activity is monitored online through a Shannon entropy-based analysis of hand-object interactions. Furthermore, the framework can recognize anomalies in human execution and autonomously trigger corrective robot actions. The approach was validated through a pilot study and a multi-subject experiment involving 14 participants. Results demonstrate the potential of such an allocation strategy for enabling intuitive and engaging collaboration without increasing the perceived workload.

title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
summary: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. However, such adaptation can substantially alter base VLM weights and degrade general visual capabilities. We introduce ZeroVLN, a slow-fast navigation framework that achieves effective navigation with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain. Rather than teaching the brain to predict geometric goals, we equip it with a semantic tool-calling interface for conveying movement decisions to an action expert in natural language. We first adapt the action expert to carry out these movement requests, then jointly improve the brain's movement decisions and the action expert's continuous execution through closed-loop reinforcement learning (RL). Trained on the same navigation episodes, ZeroVLN substantially outperforms representative SFT-based hierarchical VLN methods on standard VLN-CE (continuous environments) benchmarks, while inducing only minor changes to the brain's weights and largely preserving its general capabilities. To our knowledge, ZeroVLN is the first slow-fast VLN framework with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain, and the first to jointly optimize its slow and fast policies through closed-loop agentic RL in VLN-CE.

AI.tldr: 代表性强视觉语言导航方法需在导航数据上微调 VLM 大脑，可能改变其权重并削弱通用视觉能力。ZeroVLN 用语义工具调用接口取代几何目标预测，在 VLM 大脑零导航域 SFT 的前提下，通过闭环强化学习联合优化慢速大脑与快速动作专家，作者称在标准 VLN-CE 基准上大幅优于基于 SFT 的分层 VLN 方法。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出：典型 VLN 方法把 VLM 大脑与可学习动作头耦合，并在导航域数据上微调 VLM 大脑以预测几何目标；作者认为这种适配会显著改变基础 VLM 权重、损害其通用视觉能力。因此需要一个不在导航域对大脑做监督微调的导航方案。

title: JARVIS: An Agent That Designs, Builds, and Tests Circuit Boards on Its Own
summary: Power electronics is central to the energy transition, but developing new hardware still relies on human-led design, fabrication, testing, and iteration. We present JARVIS, an embodied AI agent that autonomously closes this loop for circuit boards. JARVIS maintains machine-specific capabilities and constraints, scans its workspace using a robot-mounted 3D scanner, and constructs an executable digital twin in which it rehearses robot motions, fabrication steps, and circuit behavior before consuming materials. A single text instruction initiates the physical experiment. Using unmodified desktop equipment, the agent coordinates a robot arm, a PCB printer that deposits conductive silver ink and solder paste, and a pick-and-place machine. It verifies progress using cameras and sensors, then tests the fabricated circuit with an OPAL-RT real-time simulator and an oscilloscope. Based on the measurements, JARVIS diagnoses deviations from the design and generates a revised design in KiCad for subsequent rehearsal. In a demonstration involving a 60 Hz notch filter for grid-connected converter sensing, JARVIS completed a first-run experiment in 2 h 39 min without human intervention, achieving 50.6 dB attenuation at 60 Hz. Its digital-twin rehearsal identified five issues before fabrication, including a test criterion that would have incorrectly rejected a functioning board. During execution, the agent also resolved encountered faults autonomously. These results demonstrate an integrated agent-driven workflow for physical design, fabrication, measurement, and iterative improvement of power-electronic circuitry. To our knowledge, JARVIS is the first system in power electronics in which an agent closes the physical design-build-test-learn loop for circuit boards.

title: Learning Ankle Exoskeleton Control for Reactive Standing Balance Through Neuromusculoskeletal Simulation
summary: Deficits in reactive balance can increase fall risk among older adults and individuals with neuromuscular impairments, motivating the need for interventions that improve balance recovery. Wearable robotic exoskeletons offer a promising approach to addressing this need by augmenting balance control. However, developing controllers that deliver appropriately timed and scaled assistance remains challenging, as evaluating each candidate strategy requires repeated exposure to destabilizing perturbations. We propose a simulation-to-real framework that combines motion imitation and reinforcement learning to develop balance-assistive ankle exoskeleton control. A muscle-driven neuromusculoskeletal model was trained using a small set of motion-capture data from a single subject to reproduce kinematic and kinetic responses to backward-translation perturbations. This model served as a virtual human for training a reinforcement-learning exoskeleton controller. The resulting controller generated bilateral ankle assistance using only inertial sensor measurements, without explicit perturbation detection. We implemented the controller on-board a bilateral ankle exoskeleton and evaluated it in five healthy subjects whose data were not used for training. Assistance increased the perturbation magnitude that subjects could withstand without stepping by 11.8% and reduced peak center-of-mass displacement and velocity by 13.5% and 28.2%, respectively. Individual benefits varied with baseline recovery strategy and body mass. These results indicate that a single virtual human can yield transferable balance assistance, and that more diverse virtual humans could further improve its effectiveness.

title: I See You: Initial Multi-Robot LiDAR Registration with Mutual-Observation Checks
comment: Accepted final version. IEEE International Symposium on Safety, Security, and Rescue Robotics (SSRR), Incheon, South Korea, November 2026. Project page: this https URL
summary: Compared to single-robot deployments, multi-robot teams can significantly improve search-and-rescue (SAR) mission success by covering large areas in parallel. To collaborate effectively, these robots must be registered in a common reference frame. Standard registration methods typically rely on external infrastructure or significant map overlap, but real deployments require infrastructure-free, stationary initial alignment for immediate operation. While global LiDAR point cloud registration addresses this, existing single-scan methods often fail silently in aliased or degenerate environments. Approaches scaling beyond two agents also remain rarely evaluated in real-world scenarios. We propose a centralized, deployment-ready framework for pre-mission multi-robot registration. Our system performs pairwise coarse-to-fine alignment and actively rejects impossible pose hypotheses via deterministic plausibility checks. We validate the framework on a real-world custom dataset of four synchronized robots in various environments with ground truth. The checks reject more than a third of the incorrect pairwise registrations while falsely rejecting less than 1% of the correct ones, and reduce the number of team registrations with a wrong robot pose by 38%. Dataset and code are publicly available.

title: Old-School Planners Drive (Sometimes) Better Than Learned Ones
summary: End-to-end driving models learn to plan from data, and hand-written planners are widely treated as a thing of the past. We test whether this is justified: we implement sixteen textbook planners, each combining a path source (reference line, A*, hybrid A*, RRT*) with a trajectory method (Frenet lattice, nonlinear optimization, $s$--$t$ search, dynamic window), and evaluate them on three benchmarks: open loop on nuScenes, closed loop on nuPlan with ground-truth perception, and photorealistic closed loop on HUGSIM. On HUGSIM, they replace only the planner of the end-to-end model UniAD and read its frozen perception, without an HD map or other privileged information. On nuScenes and nuPlan, the best textbook planners are competitive (L2 error of 0.735\,m against 0.947\,m for UniAD's planner; a nuPlan score of 79.3 against 76.1 for the rule-based PDM-Closed on Test14-hard with reactive agents). On HUGSIM, nine of the sixteen score above UniAD's learned planner on the same perception,. The best, a hybrid A* path followed by nonlinear trajectory optimization, raises HUGSIM's driving score (HD-Score) from 32.0 to 41.8. The gain is largest with standing and oncoming cars; against cars that steer at the ego, there is none. title: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots
summary: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. PLANTA uses an ontology expressed in the Web Ontology Language to represent architectural alternatives and their associated functional and quality requirements, while the Planning Domain Definition Language defines task actions and mission goals. By automatically translating and integrating these models, PLANTA enables joint planning of task and reconfiguration actions. The approach uses satisficing planning and replans when changes during execution invalidate the current plan. PLANTA is evaluated in two robotic scenarios involving underwater inspection and ground navigation. The results support the feasibility of runtime co-adaptation and show lower planning time and memory consumption compared with optimal-policy generation in the evaluated navigation scenario, while producing plans of similar quality.

AI.tldr: PLANTA 用本体（OWL）描述机器人架构备选方案、PDDL 描述任务动作与目标，自动翻译整合两套模型后联合规划任务与重构动作，并在执行中变化使计划失效时重规划。作者称在水下巡检与地面导航两个场景中验证了运行时协同自适应的可行性，且导航场景的规划时间与内存低于最优策略生成。

title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
summary: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. However, realizing this opportunity requires scaling experience banks, introducing substantial storage and search overhead that challenges the capacity, bandwidth, and power constraints of edge systems. We propose FlashX, a CMOS Directly Bonded to Array (CBA)-based NAND flash architecture for scalable experience reuse in embodied agents. FlashX exploits CBA's high internal bandwidth for parallel pSLC key search, employing interleaved Compute-in-Flash (CIF) engines to sustain sensing throughput while retaining dense TLC latent storage. Proprioception-aware clustering further reduces search overhead and enables incremental experience acquisition without global reclustering. Evaluations across VLA and WAM workloads demonstrate up to 12.24\%p and 7.43\%p improvements in task success under dense and compute-efficient configurations, respectively. FlashX achieves 2.57$\times$ higher search throughput than the strongest prior NAND search architecture under pSLC sensing, with a further 9.7$\times$ search reduction through clustering. This delivers 1.29--3.95$\times$ end-to-end speedup and 1.12--2.34$\times$ energy efficiency improvement over SSD-based retrieval.

AI.tldr: 为让 VLA/WAM 智能体在分布外环境更准确且更省算力，作者提出用 CBA 键合 NAND 闪存做并行 pSLC 经验键搜索，并用检索到的成功经验热启动 DiT 去噪；作者报告任务成功率最高提升 12.24%p 与 7.43%p，搜索吞吐较最强先前 NAND 搜索架构高 2.57×。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，具身智能体借 VLA 与世界动作模型（WAM）通过 DiT 迭代去噪生成动作，但现有模型难以泛化到分布外（OOD）环境。作者观察到检索成功经验并用于热启动去噪可帮助智能体适应陌生情境、同时降低计算开销，从而让准确率与推理效率同向改善；但这一机会要求扩展经验库，带来边缘系统难以承受的存储、带宽与功耗压力。
AI.method: 输入是智能体经验库中的成功经验（以键进行检索）与本体感知信息；方法改变的是经验的存储与检索硬件路径，而非重新训练策略网络。FlashX 是基于 CMOS 直接键合到阵列（CBA）的 NAND 闪存架构：利用 CBA 的高内部带宽执行并行 pSLC 键搜索，用交错的 Compute-in-Flash（CIF）引擎维持感知吞吐，同时保留高密度的 TLC 潜在存储；本体感知感知聚类进一步压缩搜索开销，并支持增量式经验获取而无需全局重聚类。输出是检索到的成功经验，被用于热启动 DiT 迭代去噪以生成动作，并降低推理计算开销。摘要所述对比对象为 SSD 检索方案与最强先前 NAND 搜索架构。

AI.conclusion: 若作者报告成立，其意义在于把"经验复用"从纯算法技巧扩展为存储—搜索协同设计问题：通过硬件层并行键搜索与聚类，使 OOD 任务成功率与推理效率同时改善，而非用精度换速度。证据边界明确：全部数字来自摘要自述，未说明仿真或真机、未给出硬件平台与统计细节，因此不能推断实际边缘部署表现，也不能判断收益有多少来自热启动去噪、多少来自存储架构本身。

title: A Practical Proprioceptive Data Collection Utility for the Unitree GO1
summary: The Unitree Go1 is a widely used platform for legged robotics research, yet collecting proprioceptive data from it is unnecessarily difficult: the Unitree SDK is sparsely documented, and ROS1 (Robot Operating System), the Go1's native middleware, is fully deprecated. We present an open-source graphical utility that enables researchers to reliably record proprioceptive data from the Go1, including joint states, IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit) readings, foot force sensor data, and gyroscope measurements, without requiring ROS expertise. The tool provides a simple GUI (Graphical User Interface) for starting, stopping, and labeling recordings in real time. The contribution of this paper is the collection utility. We characterize the acquisition quality of 51 recordings collected with it, including the achieved sampling rate and repeated samples. As a secondary, deliberately modest check that the data is useful, we train a terrain classifier on it. The results are weak: a Temporal Convolutional Network reaches about 38% accuracy on held-out recordings across ten terrain classes (10% would be chance), and a window-level split that ignores recording boundaries inflates the same measurement to about 99%. We report this as a demonstration that the logged signals carry terrain information, not as a competitive classifier. The utility is designed to lower the barrier to collecting Go1 proprioceptive data without ROS.

title: MIR-Depth: Multi-Range Refinement for Single-View RGB-D Depth Completion of Transparent Objects
summary: Recovering accurate visible-surface depth from a single RGB-D image and an object mask is essential for robotic grasping and manipulation of transparent objects. Specular reflections cause missing depth, while refraction corrupts nonzero returns with background depth, making raw measurements unreliable as surface anchors. Under a fixed sampling budget, refining an initial single-view prediction within a single search interval either misses large refraction offsets or sacrifices fine local resolution. To resolve this single-view trade-off, MIR-Depth constructs Coordinate-Aware Multi-Range Hypotheses: a 3D-aggregated global inverse-depth volume and depth-axis-filtered pixel-wise local volumes around a prior-guided initial depth. Selective Recurrent Refinement then introduces out-of-bounds lookup masking and validity-masked softmax fusion to iteratively update inverse depth from these volumes using a multi-scale ConvGRU. Finally, Spatially Gated Correction applies a learned per-pixel spatial gate to the full-resolution residual, preserving accurate initial geometry without imposing raw sensor readings as hard constraints. Experiments on TransCG, TODD, TRansPose, ClearPose, and HouseCat6D show that MIR-Depth achieves lower error than ReMake, DFNet, BP-Net, and PSD. Real-robot evaluations confirm accurate surface geometry for 6-DoF grasp pose prediction. Code and pretrained models will be publicly available.

title: SCCV-6D: Sparse Canonical Coordinate Voting for Holistic Multi-View RGB-D 6D Pose Estimation in Robotic Bin Picking
comment: to appear in Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV), 2027
summary: Industrial bin picking requires pose estimates that are accurate under clutter, partial occlusion, and the reflective, texture-less nature of manufactured parts. Most recent approaches to 6D pose estimation follow multi-stage pipelines. These achieve high accuracy, but incur memory and runtime footprints that do not cope with the operational constraints of many real-world industrial deployments. Holistic pipelines estimate poses in a single pass, with cost controlled through indiscriminate subsampling or lowered resolution. Continuing this line, we present SCCV-6D, a fully sparse multi-view RGB-D estimator. We reconstruct the 3D space at millimeter precision, prune background via a staged heatmap mechanism, and predict class, translation offset and rotation at highest resolution for an arbitrary number of objects simultaneously. Rotation is formulated as canonical coordinate voting. Points vote for their canonical object coordinates with an associated confidence, enabling closed-form pose recovery with a symmetry-aware weighted Procrustes solve. Along an in-cluster point recovery induced by offset votes, this removes time-consuming post-processing stages. We reuse the task-supervised attention priors from the heatmap formulation for a novel attention-gated distillation objective that reweights teacher-student feature alignment. On the IPD test split we report competitive 0.826 AP at 1.13 s per scene, significantly faster than the leading entries. On MV-YCB our approach reaches 96.1 ADD-S, and remains competitive even on the densely packed bins of ROBI.

title: ContextRenderer: Dynamic-Context Video Generation for Interactive Game Worlds
summary: Interactive game world models separate executable world evolution from visual generation, using video models to render engine-provided scene representations into detailed observations. During sustained gameplay, however, existing generative renderers struggle to follow changing conditions while preserving visual continuity across diverse proxies and target styles. We therefore introduce ContextRenderer, an autoregressive video diffusion framework designed for both dynamic conditioning and cross-proxy generalization. It couples Dynamic-Context Learning (DCL) for chunk-level interaction supervision with Recurrent History Compression (RHC) to follow condition updates while preserving visual continuity within a bounded token budget. Across proxy representations, Cross-Representation Flow Alignment (CRFA) connects proxy reconstruction with appearance and interaction variation through a shared high-fidelity reconstruction. WorldPrism, our interaction-centric dataset constructed from agent-built worlds, AAA gameplay, and open-source videos, supplies the corresponding renderings and chunk-level annotations for these learning tasks. Experiments on GWM-Bench and Solar-Bench show improved reconstruction and visual quality, while qualitative results demonstrate minute-long interactive rendering under changing prompts and subject references. title: Differentiable Hydrodynamics for Whole-Body MPC of Underwater Robots
summary: Underwater vehicle-manipulator systems distribute actuation across thrusters and joint motors. Whole-body model predictive control (MPC), rather than separate vehicle and arm controllers, can coordinate both to extend the workspace and exploit the system's full kinematic capability. Doing so, however, requires a hydrodynamic model and derivatives throughout the prediction horizon. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) captures geometry-dependent forces and moments for such a model, but is too expensive to evaluate online. We present a differentiable analytical hydrodynamic model combining smooth spherical-harmonic force and moment fields with a coupled added-inertia matrix identified from CFD. It compactly represents velocity and acceleration-dependent loads and provides their derivatives in closed form. These derivatives are propagated through free-floating vehicle--manipulator dynamics for whole-body trajectory optimization and receding-horizon control, jointly optimizing thruster forces and joint torques for reaching and continuous tracking. Held-out CFD tests validate the principal translational-force and rotational-moment fields and the added-inertia response. The analytical Jacobians evaluate faster and avoid the step-size sensitivity of central finite differences. Closed-loop Stonefish experiments demonstrate whole-body MPC in an independent marine simulator. By making geometry-dependent hydrodynamics directly available to gradient-based control, the model incorporates water forces and their sensitivities into motion allocation between the vehicle and arm, rather than treating them only as disturbances.

title: What One Sample Cannot See: Why Fewer Denoising Steps Can Score Higher on Physics Benchmarks
summary: When a storm can head north or south, a forecast down the middle may score better under squared error than either plausible path. The same paradox appears when video generators are tested as world models: fewer denoising steps can raise physics scores even as videos blur or stop moving early. Why? Physics-IQ compares each generated video with one recording, although a scene can have multiple valid futures. An exact decomposition shows its scores can reward reduced variation among generated futures, even when their distribution becomes less accurate. We introduce Kernel Physics-IQ to remove this incentive in expectation, needing only two independent samples per condition. Two-step sampling lowers Kernel Physics-IQ in all five image-to-video models. For CogVideoX, the official score rises by 0.055 while ours falls by 0.131. Changing the sampling schedule reveals further differences official scores miss. In controlled physical systems with known outcome probabilities, our metric favors the true distribution over collapsed predictions. In short, a world model should be judged not only by how closely one video matches what happened, but by how faithfully its predictions represent what could have happened.
